result.result:
The app is built and working. `npx @angular/cli@19 serve` starts it, and logging in with `admin` / `admin` lands on `/dashboard`. The production build has no errors or warnings, although I raised the per-component style warning budget from 4 kB to 6 kB because the dashboard stylesheet went over by 28 bytes.

**What I tested:** a Playwright script ran the whole flow in Chrome with no console errors:
- **Guards:** going to `/users` while logged out redirects to `/login`.
- **Login:** empty and wrong-credential submits show errors on the fields, and a correct login writes `isLoggedIn` and redirects.
- **Profile menu:** opens leftward inside the viewport (x 1036–1216 of 1280) and closes on an outside click. Sign Out clears the flag and goes to `/login`.
- **Users table:** editing a member (PUT), deleting one via Edit → Delete user (DELETE) and inviting one (POST) each showed up in the table. The details dialog opens and closes, the delete dialog closes on a backdrop click, and required-field errors show in the invite form.
- **Dashboard:** a new log line appears every 3 s.

**Where I went with S0 over Figma.** The Figma frames were available and I read them in full, but they contradict S0 on content in several places. I kept S0's wording and Figma's structure:
- **Login:** Figma shows a "Blueprint" title and a divider. I used S0's seven elements only.
- **Dashboard:** Figma has 7 tiles with different values and a combined chart/summary card. I built S0's 8 tiles with S0's values, laid out as Figma's rows: four KPIs, then Service Health (narrow) beside Request Throughput (wide), then Data Summary beside System Logs.
- **Kept from Figma, not in S0:** the "System Overview" heading with a last-updated line, an "Online" tag in the header, and a "Live" tag on the logs.
- **Users table:** Figma combines avatar and name into one "User" column. I used S0's separate columns, and Joined uses Figma's "Jan 2024" date format.
- **Footer:** S0's link columns are included even though the Figma footer is a single row.

**Where the design system couldn't express the design:**
- **Dropdowns in dialogs:** the modal body clips the role dropdown's menu, so only "Admin" was visible. Neither component has a setting for this, so I added one override scoped to the Edit and Invite dialogs (`users.component.css`). It's worth reporting to the component library.
- **Header:** `dsb-header` has no slot for extra content, so the profile control is laid over it in a box of the same width. Below about 450 px wide the header's nav doesn't collapse and ends up behind the profile control. I left that as is.
- **No token exists for:**
  - font family: I used Inter from Figma, and a generic monospace stack for the logs
  - card shadows: omitted
  - 12 px corner radius: used 10 px
  - 20 px and 26 px text: used 18 px and 22 px
  - chart and log-panel heights: calculated from the nearest size token

  I didn't approximate any of these with raw values. There are no hex/rgb colours and no `--ds-component-*` or tier-1 tokens in app code.
- **Log viewer:** it has a light background, not a dark terminal, because the status text colours don't have enough contrast on dark.
- **Modal size:** the library's modal padding and 540 px width are used as they are, instead of Figma's 560 px with divider lines.

The Angular 19 project was generated into this directory, and the dsb packages are listed in `package.json`.
